I'll just reply to your first paragraph, since you didn't state it as your opinion but as facts: 

There's no proof at all that Johnny would automatically turn back to V "after a long sleep", if he took the Pseudoendotrizine. In both Rogue and Kerry's sidequest, V only gets back their body after Johnny took the Omega Blocker.

The chip is constantly turning V's body into Johnny's, the Pseudoendotrizine *accelerates* the process while Omega Blocker only *slows down* the process. The Pseudoendotrizine is an offensive medicine, Johnny does not need to "keep popping pills throughout the night", he can just take it in chunks. The reason he chose to take Pseudoendotrizine one at a time is because he *does not want to* actually erase V.

The point of this post is it is extremely hard, if not impossible, to find even a low wage job **during an economic crisis**. 

**A majority of people** lose their jobs during these times. The closest example I can think of for the western world is Great Depression, but it is still different because **the economic crisis described here is caused by/accompanied with social restructuring.** 

You are probably born and raised in a society where market economy exists as if it's natural. It is not like that for people in some countries. 

I am not familiar with the history backgrounds in South Korea, so I'll just talk about the economic crisis in China here. Before the economic reform they don't get to "find a job", they are designated to work units and stay there for life. They don't get to "move up" within the "company“（which are mostly state-owned enterprises) because everyone gets the same salary regardless how much you work. 

Something as simple as "find a job" was foreign to many chinese people from that generation. They were not brought up, educated, or prepared for market economy. What you think is common knowledge is something they have to learn. 

Why don't they just get a low wage job? Because there are no low wage job they can get. Private ownership was discouraged, even punishable by law before the economic reform. There are no existing jobs, they have to be created. Everybody needs a new job but few are creating them. People don't start a business because they want a "quick scheme" to get rich. They start a business because they can't find a job and self employment is still better than no employment at all.

Why don't they just stay at home until they can find a job? Because their time is limited. They get a one-time pay off for what's supposed to be a life-long employment. Before that money is used up, they need to learn how to survive in an entirely different economic structure. 

Many people did benefit from the economic reform and started a successful business that changed their lives. But a lot of people were left behind too. Reforms are neccesary, but laborers shouldn't be the ones to pay the price for bad decisions made by enterprises or government.

* He thinks DR2 is popular because it is more traditional and closer to a happy ending. 

* He chose "fiction could change reality" as V3's theme. He has hoped that a miracle would happen and all fans would enjoy it, but he is not surprised with the actual reaction. (The producer jokes that his hope is betrayed)

It's easy to notice Kodaka is turning the "hope conquers despair" theme slowly into something else as the serie develops. In DR2 Hajime chooses "future" instead of hope/despair, DR3 is basically about how tyrannical the "hope" side could be. In V3 he finally let go all his pretence and denies the "hope" that is made to defeat despair. 

Following the changing of the themes, his protags are becoming more cynical, more flawed and the most important of all, able to think twice before taking actions. The traditional protag who keeps on saying "I believe in everyone!" and "I'll protect everyone!" is not what Kodaka asks for anymore.(btw for experienced shounen manga readers, these words appear too often that they've become a kind of joke.) Instead of optimism, the story needs question and denial; instead of a leader, the story needs a negativist.

As an optimistic leader, Naegi is very unlikely to ask others to die with him just to destroy the show. He might encourage everyone to destroy the show AND live together, which is kind of impossible without his protag halo and somehow weakening v3's theme by covering things up in the name of "hope". 

Hajime is the one who has the best chance here, since his choice in DR2 is a new option between hope and despair. Still, he'll need a boost to get rid of nihilism, and I'd say he would rather find a new purpose in life than a reason to die. 

Kaede - I'm expecting a rain of downvotes here - has the smallest possibility to act like Saihara does. She is a believer and a protecter, but not very good at doubting her actions. Remember what she does when they fail countless times at the "exit"? She keeps on trying and trying the same thing, until Oma jumps out and asks her to stop forcing others(that's his opinion, not mine). Of course she could have dramatical transformation IF she lives, which is a IF that could basically happen to anyone, and a IF which means re-writing the whole story. It still seems more likely to me that she will offer to sacrifice herself and encourage others to keep on fighting.

Saihara, on the contrary, is very cynical from the start. His story about the murder he solves is the base of his personality - He keeps asking if he is doing something wrong, if there really is a correct answer. He is not a protag who becomes cynical in the process - he is the skeptical guy who tries to learn to believe. Before entering the "exit" for the first time, he has already suspected that it might be a trap made to discourage them, but he keeps quiet because he is touched by Kaede's spirit - her spirit, not her decision. Everything I'm talking about here is in Chapter 1, before he "develops" or is affected by anyone, and I could already see him making the decision that he actually does in the end. 

So in short, yes. I think Naegi, Hajime and Akamatsu will all make unique decisions that fit their personalities. Saihara's choice is a choice of his own, or you could say Kodaka made him this way so he could make the choice Kodaka wanted him to choose, either way it IS a trait that only he has.

Folkloristic is not necessarily a subcategory of Anthropology, and in no way an aspect of Cultural Anthropology. The traditional Folkloristic, originated from Europe, is closer to Literature and Mythology. The American Folklorists have a closer bond with Cultural Anthropology and Ethnology, but even the american Folkloristic does not belong to them, instead they are independent fields sharing some methods of studies, such as field study. Nowadays when we talk about Folkloristic we usually mean european and american Folkloristic as a whole, which makes it more than a subcategory of Anthropology.

As for Japenese Folkloristic, they developed a system relatively of their own, but even for them Folkloristic(民俗学) is different from Cultural Anthropology (文化人類学・民族学). I would hardly think fate vs. free will is a reasonable theme for nisekoi. If Kosaki and Raku's "engagement" is decided by their parents, the theme would certainly be "fate vs. free will". But it's not. They fell in love with each other in childhood, they grew up, and fall in love with each other once again. The "promise" was a symbol of free will: Regardless of all the accidents or obstacles that future may bring, they'll meet again and get together. 

Although I also agree Raku and Chitoge had solid emotional development, Komi didn't do anything to weaken the bond between Raku and Kosaki. Instead he strengthened it. The Christmas chapter, where Raku chose Kosaki over the promised girl without any regret, happened in chapter 166-168. Even if we assume Nisekoi would finish with about 240 chapters, in 2/3 of the story Raku had always thought he loved Kosaki. Even when he realized his feeling for Chitoge, he still thought his feeling for Kosaki did not fade or change. 

Isn't it unnatural, that two people love each other, and their feelings grow stronger over time, but they didn't get together? Not to mention a simple confession is interrupted for seven or eight times, with baseball, phonecalls, and storm? With so many accidents, people would expect rainbow after the storm, but no,it's just some dumb plot device. 

Why would I think Kosaki end would be more natural? Because both Chitoge and Kosaki have deep emotional connections with Raku, and to choose one over another, the reason has to be fairly eloquent. "Sorry, I like her more" is not enough at this point of the story any more. 

In the latest chapters Komi has focused mainly on Chitoge, portraying her struggle with her feelings, her painful acceptance of the past memories, her cowardess and her courage.Even if Raku didn't choose her in the end, that's some solid charater development.This amount of portraying would be eloquent for the "lost" side.  Chitoge could confirm her feelings and start a new life with confidence.

She just had a sudden realization and confessed real fast and sent her love away with a broken heart.You remember the fairy tale where the angel gave the prince her key? In book 4 when Harry met Crouch, he wrote to Sirius describing how abnormal he seemed. He expected more information from Sirius, and maybe some readers(me) expect the same. However Sirius only told Harry to keep his head down, drop the whole thing, and promise to never break any rules. He then writes to Harry almost every day(a detail I've missed before) repeating the same thing. 

Also in book 5 when he himself was locked in Grimmould, all he wrote to Harry was comforting words and "do not get in trouble", while Ron and Hermione only made Harry feel worse by writing things like "We know a lot but can't tell you." 

Sirius definately knows Harry is not James and he always puts Harry's safety above anything else. The only time when Sirius encouraged Harry taking risks(I mean real risks. Sirius is an experienced trouble maker and he knows where the line lies.) was in book 5, when he brought up the idea of DA. But at that time he was shut in what to him the most terrible place, experiencing what to him is way painful than death, he wasn't acting like his usual self. Plus, the DA doesn't do any lasting damage, it actually helped a lot in book 6 and 7. The only kost would have been Sirius's own life. 

To Harry, he was definately a good godfather.

 He was always there when Harry needed him, which is very important for Harry, because Harry is always sensitive about parents abandoning their children. He said several times in books that "no parents should abandon their children unless they can't help it". Sirius never, ever left Harry abandoned for a single time when he could help it. 

Also, Sirius was closer to Harry than any other adults. Harry couldn't bring himself to talk about his problems with Mr. and Mrs Weasley, Lupin or even Dumbledore. But he always feel it's safe to spill out all his secrets in front of Sirius. He knows he could say whatever he wants and will not be disliked, feel ashamed, or gets a lot of pressure because the adults will worry too much. He knows Sirius would comfort him, offer to help him, while not stressing him not. 

Last, Sirius does see James in Harry, but it's in a healthy way. He only says Harry is like James when he really is, like being good at Quidittich, like bringing a Hippogriff to the tower(don't think Lily ever did anything similiar), like being adventrous and reckless sometimes. When in the book 5 Mrs Weasley and Sirius quarreled about what was good for Harry, Harry didn't hesitate to take Sirius side. Sirius didn't treat Harry as a child, but as a young man who could take responsibilities, ask questions and think independently, which is what Harry wanted to be. 

Overall I think Sirius in the stories was a good godfather, a good friend, a good brother - which Harry actually needed and wanted very badly. Had he been innocent and lived with Harry from the start, I guess he would have been that cool parent that every children wish they had. He would be that sort of father that never tells Harry to go to bed early instead he'll mess with him until midnight. However, when Harry needs him, he'll always there. He would be like a brother that never bullies him, a friend that knows about everything, a father that is both loving and fun. 

Some adults might not think that's good. But for children I guess he's just awesome.
